q: Ten minutes after a deploy, error rates spike. You suspect the deploy but are not sure. What should you do first?
options: Read the diff line by line until you find the bug
Restart all pods to clear any bad state
Roll back the deploy to mitigate, then investigate the root cause with the pressure off
explain: Mitigate before you root-cause. Rollback is fast, well-tested and reversible; if errors stop, you have also confirmed the hypothesis. Debugging live extends the outage.

q: A pod shows `CrashLoopBackOff`. `kubectl logs <pod>` prints only startup lines. Which command most likely shows why it crashed?
explain: After a crash the container restarts, so plain `logs` shows the new instance. `--previous` shows the output of the instance that died. Deleting the pod destroys that evidence.

q: A container's Last State is `Terminated`, Reason `OOMKilled`, Exit Code 137, and the Node app logged no error. Which statement is correct?
options: V8 ran out of heap; raise `--max-old-space-size`
The image has the wrong architecture
The kernel killed the process for exceeding the container memory limit; off-heap memory such as Buffers counts too
explain: 137 = SIGKILL. The cgroup OOM killer counts total RSS (heap + Buffers + native). A V8 heap exhaustion instead prints `JavaScript heap out of memory` and exits 134, with reason `Error`.

q: All requests return 503 from the Gateway. Pods are `Running` with `0/1` READY and zero restarts. What do you check first?
options: The readiness probe failure message in `kubectl describe pod` and the Service's ready endpoints
explain: Not Ready with no restarts means readiness is failing (liveness would cause restarts). With no ready endpoints the proxy answers 503 itself. The probe failure message tells you whether it is the probe config or a dependency.

q: After `kubectl rollout undo` restored service in Drill 3, why is the incident not fully resolved?
options: `rollout undo` only restores the pod template; `spec.strategy: Recreate` remains and the next deploy will again drop all pods at once
The Service selector was also changed
explain: Deployment-level fields such as `strategy`, `replicas` and `progressDeadlineSeconds` are not part of the pod template, so undo does not touch them. Always check the full diff against a known-good manifest.

q: A default-deny NetworkPolicy was applied an hour ago and nothing broke. After a routine deploy, the API cannot reach Postgres. Which explanations fit? (select all)
options: DNS egress may also be missing, which would show up as name resolution failures
Many implementations enforce policies on new connections, so existing pooled connections kept working until pods restarted
There is no egress rule from the API pods to Postgres and/or no ingress rule on the Postgres pods
NetworkPolicies only take effect after 60 minutes
explain: Policies are allow-lists needing both egress (client) and ingress (server) rules; established flows can survive policy changes, delaying the impact to the next restart. Missing DNS egress is a common second cause. There is no built-in delay.

q: `kubectl get hpa` shows `cpu: <unknown>/50%` while `kubectl top pods` works. What is the most likely cause?
options: The target containers have no CPU request, so utilisation cannot be computed
explain: HPA utilisation = usage / request. `kubectl top` working proves metrics-server is fine. `kubectl describe hpa` shows `missing request for cpu`.

q: A new release fails with `exec /app/entrypoint.sh: exec format error`. Node and image architectures match. What is the likely cause?
options: The script is missing its shebang line (`#!/bin/sh`)
explain: `execve` returns ENOEXEC for a file that is neither ELF for this CPU nor a `#!` script. Missing execute permission gives `permission denied` (exit 126). The other classic cause, wrong architecture, was ruled out.

q: A StatefulSet's PVC is Pending because its `storageClassName` does not exist. What is the correct fix?
options: Delete the StatefulSet (and the stuck PVC), fix the class in the manifest and recreate it, since volume claim templates are immutable
explain: Most StatefulSet spec fields, including `volumeClaimTemplates`, cannot be updated. With real data you would orphan and migrate carefully; here the claim never bound, so delete and recreate.

q: Terraform reports `Error acquiring the state lock`. The CI runner that held it crashed. What must you do before `terraform force-unlock`?
options: Prove no process or CI job is still running an operation against that state, using the lock info (who, when, operation)
explain: Unlocking a live operation allows two writers and can corrupt state. Confirm the holder is dead, then force-unlock with the lock ID and run a plan to reconcile what the interrupted apply left behind.

q: Helm says `another operation (install/upgrade/rollback) is in progress` after a CI job was killed mid-upgrade. Which are appropriate? (select all)
options: Make CI timeouts longer than Helm's `--timeout` and use `--rollback-on-failure` (Helm 4) or `--atomic` (Helm 3)
Inspect `helm history` to find the last `deployed` revision
explain: The killed upgrade left a `pending-upgrade` record that acts as a lock; rolling back clears it. Uninstalling deletes everything the release owns. The prevention is to never kill Helm mid-operation and to let failed upgrades roll back automatically.

q: Under load, pods restart repeatedly and 5xx spikes appear; at rest everything is fine. The Deployment has a 15m CPU limit and a liveness probe with `timeoutSeconds: 1`, `failureThreshold: 1`. What is happening?
options: CPU throttling slows `/healthz` past the 1 s timeout, one failure triggers a restart, which reduces capacity and amplifies the overload
The readiness probe is too lenient
explain: Aggressive liveness turns slowness into restarts, a self-amplifying failure. Remove or raise the CPU limit, set an honest request, and tune liveness to detect deadlocks (longer timeout, failureThreshold >= 3). Readiness is the tool for shedding load.

q: Which sentence best reflects a blameless postmortem?
options: "Alex forgot to run the staging tests, causing the outage."
"The pipeline allowed chart changes to merge without a staging smoke test; action: add an e2e check (owner, due date)."
"Engineers should be more careful with probes."
explain: Blameless postmortems describe how the system allowed the failure and produce owned, dated action items that change the system. "Be more careful" and "human error" change nothing.
